newsitem.title: UK: British trade deficit slashed as exports soar.
newsitem.headline: British trade deficit slashed as exports soar.

text.p: Britain's trade deficit with the rest of the world narrowed sharply in October as exports were snapped up, the government said Tuesday.
Britain's trade deficit was pared to 454 million pounds ($760.1 million) in October from 1,059 million pounds ($1.5 billion) in September, the Office for National Statistics said.

But more up-to-date figures for Britain's trade with non-European Union nations showed a deficit of 639 million pounds ($916 million) in November, well above October's 418 million pounds ($599 million) shortfall.
Treasury minister Phillip Oppenheim welcomed the figures and said they showed exports were on a strong upward path.
Britain exported goods worth 14.62 billion pounds ($20.9 billion) to the rest of the world in October. In September, total exports were just below 14 billion ($20.1 billion).
"These figures again show that growth is broadly balanced and illustrate the growing success of the British economy," Oppenheim said.
The ONS said the erratic pattern of trade figures made a trend difficult to discern. But it said its latest estimate suggested the global trade gap was narrowing.
